messages:
sarah: FYI customer Acme (ticket #12345) reports sudden 401 invalid_api_key from CI after key rotation. They say the same key works from laptop, but CI jobs fail immediately. Repro steps pasted below.

sarah: Customer repro: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX_REDACTED" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 401 
{"error":"invalid_api_key"} -- they rotated the key via the dashboard earlier today.

infra-bot: auth-service log snippet (2026-03-16T15:12:02Z):
```
[2026-03-16T15:12:02Z] INFO auth: check_key key_id=kb_ABC123 org=org-acme remote_ip=34.56.78.90 result=reject reason=ip_allowlist_mismatch
```

ashley: Okay — that log line strongly suggests the key has an IP restriction. Dashboard supports per-key IP allowlist and per-org outbound policy. Did they enable "Enforce IP allowlist" when creating the key?

mike: I pulled the key metadata from the control plane: allowed_ips: ["10.0.0.0/8"] created_by=acme-admin created_at=2026-03-16T14:55:01Z. CI runner IP 34.56.78.90 is not in that range. So 401 is expected.

mike: Quick remediation options for the customer:
- Add CI runner IPs (34.56.78.90 / 34.56.78.0/24) to the key's allowed IPs in Dashboard
- Create a new server-side key without restrictions for CI (rotate after)
- Use a short-lived token exchange from an allowed server to the CI job (recommended for security)

sarah: I messaged the customer with the three options and included exact steps for adding an allowed IP in the console (Dashboard > Settings > API keys > edit restrictions). Asked them to confirm which CI IPs to add.

customer-update (from acme ops via email quoted by Sarah): "We added 34.56.78.90 to the key's allowed IPs and retried—requests now return 200. Thanks!"

ashley: Nice. Can we add a quick note to the KB about ambiguous 401s from IP allowlists? There are a bunch of hits in support search.

mike: +1. Also adding a small CLI snippet we can paste into support replies: 
```
# check remote IP seen by Redwood when running from CI
curl -sS --header "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/remote-ip
```

sarah: Customer confirmed fix, ticket #12345 -> resolved. I left a note to suggest rotating the key after CI whitelist is confirmed and to consider short-lived tokens. :white_check_mark:

mike: marking as root cause = key created with IP allowlist that excluded CI. Leaving pointer to KB PR.

ashley: thanks team.
